title: Finiteness of a module is detected by its formal glueing data
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$ and $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$, such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Then $M$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] if and only if the base change $M\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change] is a finitely generated $S$-module and, for every $i$, the localization $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is a finitely generated $R_{f_i}$-module.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 05EU (remark-formal-glueing-algebras, line 25036), the case 'finite': R -> S x prod R_{f_i} is faithfully flat, and finiteness descends along faithfully flat maps (Algebra, Lemma 03C4, lemma-descend-properties-modules)
